title: Rest, Says the Person Who Never Rests

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks two adults)

collection.description: A villager who never rests tells a tired friend to rest: point this out, or take the advice.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has been working too hard and looks tired. (friend) sits (subject.him/her) down. "You need to rest. Take a day. Take two. Nobody will mind." (subject) looks at (friend): the person who was up before dawn, mended three nets, built half a wall and is still holding a hammer.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: "And when did YOU last rest?" asks (subject). (friend) opens (friend.his/her) mouth. Closes it. Looks at the hammer. "That's different," (friend.he/she) says. "How?" says (subject). There is a long pause. "...It's not different," (friend) admits. They both take the next afternoon off and lie in hammocks side by side. (friend) fidgets the whole time. It's a start.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) decides that good advice is good advice, no matter who gives it. (subject.He/she) takes a day off. It's wonderful. (subject.He/she) sleeps, swims, eats fruit in the shade. In the evening (subject.he/she) walks past (friend), still working by torchlight. (subject) doesn't say anything. (subject.He/she) just leaves a mango on (friend)'s step. (friend) gets the message, mostly.
